messages:
maria-sales: Quick sync — Atlas Health wants concrete numbers for a PoC. They expect ~1k concurrent active users (roughly 2k RPS) for short bursts and a steady-state of ~400 RPS. Target SLA: p95 latency <= 300ms for 256-token completions. Can we put together a runbook + cost estimate and call out any enterprise blockers?

sam-eng: got it. clarifying q: when you say 1k concurrent users, do they mean 1k concurrent connections or 1k parallel inference requests? that maps to RPS differently depending on prompt lengths.

maria-sales: they mean concurrent interactive users — assume avg 2 requests/min per user during peak -> ~33 RPS per 1k users? hmm sorry mixed numbers. For sales deck they asked for both scenarios: (A) 1k concurrent users typical chat behavior (~35 RPS) and (B) 2k RPS load test for stress/upper bound. want both numbers.

sam-eng: ok. i'll draft a dual-path plan: baseline interactive (35 RPS, 256 tokens avg) + stress (2k RPS, 128 tokens avg). plan: ramp to target over 5 min, 30 min sustained window, 5x burst tests for 2 min. will record p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, kernel stalls, and queue depth.

sam-eng: recommended model config: redwood-14b-int8 for baseline (good quality/cost), redwood-4b-quant for heavy burst fallback. enable prefix KV cache for repeated context to cut token work ~20-40% depending on UX. suggest batching target 8-16 for throughput mode.

julie-se: security question from their InfoSec: data residency + transient logs. need language: hosted API does not retain request text beyond 30 days by default and we offer private deployments with customer-managed KMS for on-prem keys. i'll attach standard answers but flag if ops needs to confirm retention.

maria-sales: pricing ask: they asked rough cost/M active user and delta if they commit to Dedicated reserved capacity. can we provide quick ballpark?

sam-eng: ballpark numbers: hosted on-demand at current perf = ~$0.75 per 1k 256-token completions (includes token + infra amortized) — for 35 RPS continuous that's ~2.3m completions/month -> rough $1.7k/mo. For 2k RPS stress runs short-lived, cost dominated by GPU time: estimate $120/hr for dedicated nodes used for burst tests; full-day stress cluster ~ $2.5k. Reserved Dedicated discounts ~30-45% depending on commit and sustained usage. (send to pricing for final numbers).

devon-ml: load test notes: please instrument to capture KV cache hit ratio + batching distribution. if cache hit >30% costs drop significantly. also run a quantized model variant to measure quality delta — we should include basic rouge/accuracy on ~50 eval prompts post-run.

sam-eng: attaching quick k6 snippet we used for earlier demos:
```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function() {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-14b-int8', input: '...prompt...', max_tokens: 256 });
  const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': `Bearer ${__ENV.API_KEY}` };
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer', payload, { headers: headers });
  sleep(0.05); // ~20 RPS per VU tweak for target
}
```
replace with their endpoint/keys; tune VU count to hit target RPS.

ops-bot: deploy log: loadtest-cluster-42 launched (gpu-pool:dedicated-burst) at 1896543500

sam-eng: ran the baseline sim earlier this morning against a 4-node dedicated pool. results (256 tokens avg): p50=90ms, p95=260ms, p99=480ms; sustained 35 RPS no queueing; cost projection matches ballpark above. burst test (2k RPS w/ batching=12): p95=420ms, p99=1.2s on peak — we saw GPU queuing and kernel contention. switching to fallback redwood-4b-quant dropped p95 to 220ms but quality regression on 12/50 eval prompts.

maria-sales: perfect — can you summarize into a 1-page for Atlas with clear asks (API key, target prompts, security Qs) and callouts: recommended Dedicated for sustained high loads, fallback model for bursts, and expected cost ranges?

sam-eng: will do. action items: sam -> one-pager + k6 script, julie -> security answers + retention snippet, devon -> eval prompts and cache instrumentation checklist. I'll also include a recommended autoscale policy: min 2 nodes, scale out when queue_depth > 50 or p95 > 300ms.

julie-se: noted. I'll also ask InfoSec if they need SOC2 artifact export for the PoC.

maria-sales: thanks team — target to ship one-pager by EOD today. Atlas kickoff weds. :white_check_mark:

sam-eng: will post the draft here once ready. :rocket:
